rules.rule: Check for urgent throat symptom conditions
rules.problem: Danger-sign check_for list matches the red box; airway obstruction/swelling listed separately here, unlike the priority rule.

rules.rule: Assess throat symptoms not needing urgent attention
rules.problem: Omits some page items: tender neck lymph nodes, mild fever, bleeding, and the 'food/liquid gets stuck, refer' step. Minor.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from throat symptoms with sudden face/tongue swelling
rules.problem: Structure faithful (throat symptom AND sudden face/tongue swelling AND any of list); possible matches 'check for anaphylaxis'. Allergen timing window dropped; BP rule encoded as systolic<90 OR diastolic<60, a reasonable reading.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable oesophageal candida from painful or difficult swallowing
rules.problem: Fires without any throat-symptom trigger or exclusion of urgent presentations; page bullet sits in the not-urgent assess box. Otherwise faithful, probable matches 'likely'.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible diphtheria from throat/nose pseudomembrane
rules.problem: Faithful: sore throat AND pseudomembrane in throat or nose; mild fever optional so correctly omitted. possible matches 'Consider'.

Flowchart logic faithful: no pseudomembrane, swollen tonsils AND (pus OR no cough OR no runny nose). Sore throat requirement is inferred from the question's 'sore throat AND pseudomembrane' No-branch; acceptable.
Is the exact complement of the bacterial branch (no swollen tonsils OR (no pus AND cough AND runny nose)), with red throat/swollen tonsils as the box descriptor. Tender neck nodes not encoded.

rules.rule: Urgent: throat symptoms with danger signs
rules.problem: Priority Urgent is justified by the red box ('Refer urgently'). But airway danger sign requires pharyngeal swelling AND obstruction, while the page says swelling blocking airway with obstruction to be assessed; may under-trigger.

summary: Rules track the page well; flowchart logic for bacterial/viral/diphtheria is faithful and the red-box danger signs are all present with correct role and Urgent priority. Most consequential: the airway danger sign ANDs pharyngeal swelling with confirmed upper respiratory obstruction although the page says to assess for obstruction, so it may under-trigger. Minor: allergen-exposure concepts drop the past-few-hours window, candida rule has no throat-symptom precondition, and a few page items (tender nodes, fever, stuck food refer) are not encoded.
